# CYW43455 firmware & NVRAM provenance (EAIDK-310)

Policy: **no proprietary wireless firmware blobs are committed to this
repository.**  The blobs live only on the board's `/lib/firmware/` and
are documented here by filename, SHA-256 and origin so the deployment
stays reproducible without redistributing them.

## Origin

The complete `/lib/firmware/` tree on the board was carried over from
the factory image (openailab Fedora 28, image files dated 2024-03-12,
owned by the board's `Fog` account after the Debian migration).  It is
a Rockchip/Ampak-style vendor firmware pack:

- `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.{bin,txt,clm_blob}` — CYW43455 SDIO set,
- `brcm/BCM4345C5.hcd` — CYW43455 Bluetooth patchram,
- `fw_bcm43455c0_ag{,_apsta,_p2p}.bin`, `nvram_ap6255.txt` — the vendor
  DHD-driver naming for the same module,
- `regulatory.db*` — wireless-regdb content.

**None of these files is owned by a Debian package** (`dpkg -S` finds no
owner); the Debian-looking `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.*` names are the
factory pack's own.  Upstream redistributability of the factory pack is
not established, hence the no-commit rule above.

Key fact discovered during P9: the board's
`brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.txt` is **byte-identical** to the factory
`nvram_ap6255.txt` (same SHA-256 below).  The NVRAM that brcmfmac will
request is therefore this board's own factory NVRAM — no foreign-board
NVRAM is needed (no `FOREIGN_NVRAM_TEST_ONLY` case applies).

## Request names (authoritative source = kernel logs)

Expected once SDIO enumerates (to be confirmed in
`docs/P9-BRCMFMAC-PROBE.md` when the candidate boots):

- `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.bin`,
- `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.<compatible>.txt` fallback chain ending in
  `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.txt`,
- `brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.clm_blob`,
- BT (hci_bcm, ROM-dependent): `brcm/BCM4345C5.hcd` — confirm from the
  actual `hci0: bcm: patch` log line, do not assume.

## Deployment rule

The firmware stays board-local.  If a reproducible installer is ever
needed it must (a) fetch from an upstream source whose license permits
redistribution (e.g. Debian `firmware-brcm80211` / `linux-firmware`
cypress set), (b) pin the package version and SHA-256s, and (c) refuse
to run when the hashes drift.  It must not extract blobs from this git
history, because there are none.
